name: קְטוּרָה
summary: The wife Abraham took after Sarah's death (Gen 25:1), called his concubine in Chronicles (1Ch 1:32). She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah, the fathers of Sheba, Dedan and the Midianites (Gen 25:2–4); Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from Isaac, east, to the land of the east (Gen 25:6). The name has the form of a passive of the root, “made fragrant, perfumed”, as the pual מְקֻטֶּרֶת “perfumed with myrrh and frankincense” (Sng 3:6); scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Abraham took another wife, and her name was קְטוּרָה.”
“All these were the sons of Keturah.”
The sons of the concubines sent away east with gifts.
The pual participle מְקֻטֶּרֶת “perfumed” with myrrh and frankincense: the passive sense the name's form suggests.

note: Takes s.bg.ad (4 tokens). The reading “perfumed” takes the name as a passive form of the smoke/incense sense; a reading from the other sense, “bound”, is also possible (rabbinic plays on both are no evidence). No verse gives the meaning.
